record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How do client-sampling constraints and decentralized data collection affect fairness in federated learning, and under what assumptions can fairness-improving methods from centralized learning be adapted to the federated setting?

evidence.quote: Future work could investigate the degree to which these various sampling constraints affect the fairness of the resulting model, and how such impacts can be mitigated within the federated framework ... Adapting such solutions to the federated learning setting and further improving upon them will be challenging research questions in ML fairness theory and algorithms. ... It is an open question whether such approaches, which have demonstrated utility for improving fairness in centralized training, could be used under the setting of federated learning ...

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning system consisting of a central server and a population of clients $\mathcal{C} = \{1,2,\dots,N\}$. Each client $i \in \mathcal{C}$ holds a local data distribution $\mathcal{D}_i$ over an input-label-attribute space $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{A}$, where $\mathcal{A}$ encodes a protected attribute (e.g. demographic group). At each round $t$, a (possibly biased) sampling mechanism selects a subset $S_t \subseteq \mathcal{C}$ of clients according to a distribution $q_t$ that may depend on availability constraints, device characteristics, network connectivity, time zone, or other systematic factors that cause $q_t$ to deviate from the uniform distribution. The server then aggregates locally trained updates from clients in $S_t$ to produce a global model $h:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}$.

Fix a fairness criterion $\mathcal{F}(h)$ for centralized learning (e.g. demographic parity, equalized odds, calibration, or individual fairness with respect to a metric on $\mathcal{X}$), defined as a functional of $h$ and a global data distribution $\mathcal{D}^* = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \mathcal{D}_i$. Suppose that in the centralized setting (where a learner has direct sample access to $\mathcal{D}^*$) there exists a known algorithm $\mathcal{A}_{\text{cen}}$ that produces a model $h$ achieving $\mathcal{F}(h) \le \varepsilon$ while attaining utility within $\delta$ of the unconstrained optimum.

Address the following:

1. Quantify, as a function of the divergence between $q_t$ and the uniform distribution and of the heterogeneity among the $\mathcal{D}_i$, how client-sampling bias and decentralized data collection degrade $\mathcal{F}(h)$ for the model produced by standard federated aggregation (e.g. FedAvg).

2. Identify minimal assumptions on (a) the sampling distributions $\{q_t\}$, (b) the inter-client heterogeneity (e.g. bounded $\chi^2$ or KL divergence between $\mathcal{D}_i$ and $\mathcal{D}^*$), (c) the availability of protected-attribute information at clients or server, and (d) the communication and privacy constraints (such as differential privacy or secure aggregation), under which $\mathcal{A}_{\text{cen}}$ can be adapted into a federated algorithm $\mathcal{A}_{\text{fed}}$ that, with high probability, returns a global model $h$ satisfying $\mathcal{F}(h) \le \varepsilon + o(1)$ while preserving utility within $\delta + o(1)$ of the federated optimum.

3. Either construct such an adaptation $\mathcal{A}_{\text{fed}}$ for a representative class of fairness criteria, or prove an impossibility result showing that under the stated constraints no federated algorithm can simultaneously achieve approximate fairness, approximate utility, and the required privacy/communication guarantees.
artifact.status_search_result: Fairness under client-sampling bias in federated learning remains an active research area. Subsequent works (e.g., q-FFL, AFL, FairFed, and various papers on fairness-aware federated optimization through 2023–2025) have proposed partial solutions for specific fairness notions and sampling models, but a general theory characterizing when centralized fairness algorithms can be lifted to the federated setting under heterogeneity, biased participation, and privacy/communication constraints is not yet established. The problem is therefore considered open in its general form.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists adapting centralized fairness solutions to federated learning, under sampling bias, as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The general question of how sampling constraints affect fairness and how to adapt centralized fairness methods to FL is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: FairFed: Enabling Group Fairness in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a federated method for group fairness with heterogeneous clients, providing partial empirical solutions but not a general theory.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for specific group-fairness notions, indicating the broader question is still open.
